prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Document units:
S781: The Identity Access Service shall support rapid suspension of accounts when a user changes role, leaves an organization, or becomes subject to an operational integrity concern.
S782: Temporary access shall have a defined sponsor, purpose, role scope, and expiry time, and shall be reviewed after the operational need has ended.
S783: Silverpine shall accept emergency access activations only after the Identity Access Service records the authorizing incident reference and expiry time.
S784: Emergency access may be granted to the Emergency Response Coordinator, Airport Duty Manager, or System Support Engineer when life safety, airport continuity, or critical system recovery requires immediate action.
S785: Use of emergency access shall generate prominent audit events and shall require post-event review by the Data Governance Steward and the responsible operational authority.
S786: During Contingency Fallback State, access control shall continue to enforce role separation even when some integrations are unavailable and manual coordination becomes necessary.
S787: When normal connectivity is restored, the Regional Flow Platform shall reconcile contingency actions with the Collaborative Decision Log so that accountability is preserved across the full incident timeline.
S788: After connectivity is restored, audit processing shall treat reconciled contingency actions as part of the same operational record as actions taken during Normal Operations.
S789: The Regional Flow Platform shall record slot compliance events in the Audit Event Ledger using the operating date, flight identifier, airport, runway direction, and applicable regulation reference.
S790: Each compliance assessment shall compare the Calculated Takeoff Time, the Target Off Block Time, actual off-block time, and actual takeoff time against the tolerance defined in the Business Rules Registry.
S791: The Slot Compliance State shall indicate whether a flight was compliant, early, late, exempted, substituted, cancelled, or pending review at the end of the traffic period.
S792: The Audit Event Ledger shall preserve the time source applied by the Time Synchronization Service so that later review can distinguish operational delay from data latency.
S793: User decisions entered through the Airport CDM Portal shall be linked to the authenticated role provided by the Identity Access Service.
S794: The Collaborative Decision Log shall retain the stated reason, decision time, affected flight, and visible operational context for each material change to a slot or sequence.
S795: The Airline Operations Coordinator uses the permission email to justify an approved slot substitution during post-operations review.
S796: Substitution records shall show the original flight, replacement flight, assigned Calculated Takeoff Time, acceptance status, and any subsequent cancellation or reversion.
S797: When an Aircraft Operator Representative proposes a substitution, the audit trail shall capture whether the change preserved the constraints of the active Ground Delay Program.
S798: The Slot Coordinator shall review substitution activity after operations to confirm that priority rules were applied consistently across participating operators.
S799: Late operational changes shall be distinguished from planned updates by comparing the change timestamp with the freeze horizon held in the Business Rules Registry.
S800: Changes made inside the freeze horizon shall require a reason code and shall be visible to the Regional Flow Manager during post-operations review.
S801: The Tower Sequence Manager and Ramp Movement Board shall provide actual movement milestones that support independent verification of slot performance.
S802: Surface movement evidence from the Surface Surveillance Adapter shall be retained long enough to support dispute resolution and regulatory audit requests.
S803: Capacity changes made through the Capacity Assessment Module shall be correlated with the active Airport Capacity Plan and Airport Acceptance Rate used at the time of allocation.
S804: The Performance Analytics Warehouse shall aggregate compliance outcomes by carrier, route group, regulation, airport operating configuration, and time band.
S805: Aggregated metrics shall support review of systemic lateness without exposing commercially sensitive detail beyond authorized roles.
S806: The Data Governance Steward shall verify that audit fields required for slot performance reporting remain complete, immutable, and traceable to approved data definitions.
S807: The System Support Engineer shall investigate technical gaps when audit sequences show missing events, duplicate updates, or inconsistent timestamps.
S808: The Regional Flow Manager shall use the Post Operations Report to identify whether noncompliance resulted from operator choice, airport constraint, airspace constraint, weather impact, or system issue.
S809: The Airport Duty Manager shall review late airport-driven changes that affected multiple flights and shall record whether the operational justification was valid.
S810: Findings from the review shall feed adjustments to tolerance values, reason code definitions, and training material, subject to change control.
S811: All audit outputs shall be retained according to the approved records schedule and shall remain searchable for compliance investigations, performance meetings, and lessons-learned activity.
S812: Data governance for the Regional Flow Platform shall assign accountable owners to each operational data domain and shall make those assignments visible in the Airport CDM Portal.
S813: The Data Governance Steward shall maintain the data ownership register and shall coordinate updates through the Business Rules Registry.
S814: The Regional Flow Manager shall own flow management policy data, including Ground Delay Program parameters and Tactical Regulation Proposal status values.
